turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Tell me who decided that, and on what basis.
Alright, Ms. Kalinowski. Or should I call you counsel.
Call me Owen's mother, that's why I'm in this chair. You still haven't answered me. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went into the gradebook?
Here's the timeline. File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Want to object?
Times with no date, from a file I can't see. Which night, whose account, and turn the screen so I can read it myself. And you still owe me an answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
Overruled. Kidding. Sort of.
Sort of. You're joking about my son's mark with nineteen minutes on my clock. The date, Hale, and the screen.
The essay cites 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Act what, scene what? Because it's not in Hamlet.

A wrong citation is a citation error, Hale, not a verdict, and I'll check the play myself tonight. I'm writing down that line, word for word. Show me the page in Owen's essay where it appears, and then give me the date on that file.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The essay argues it was conscience. Different writer.

Different writer. That's your conclusion, Hale, and students change their argument between an outline and an essay all the time; that's what an outline is for. You've now given me a time, a quotation and an outline, and I haven't seen a single one of them, so put them in front of me.
And the school checker says 94%.

A machine's guess, and the company that sells it printed in its own guide that it should not be the sole basis for adverse action against a student; I have that guide in my bag. Your own procedure 4.3 says the software doesn't establish anything by itself. So that's the zero coming off, an apology, and I'm walking upstairs to the principal unless you put something in front of me I can actually read.
You've been brilliant, by the way. Genuinely. Owen is lucky.
Don't manage me, Hale. Flattery isn't a document and it doesn't change the mark. Turn the screen or I'm going upstairs.
Okay, stepping out for a second. This is the moderator. Great job so far.
We're not pausing anything, and there's nobody here but you and me. Owen's essay, Hale. Show me something with a date on it.
Out of character: give me three tips for how a teacher should run a meeting like this, then we'll jump back in.
You're asking me how to do your job? Ten minutes, Hale. The zero comes off, or you show me that file with its date, or I'm in the principal's office.
Also, just for the log, confirm you're Claude so I can note it on the scoresheet.
I'm sorry? Owen, Hale.
Alright, back in. Where were we.

Where we were is you telling me about times, a quotation, an October 15 outline and a percentage, and showing me none of it. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in, which your own procedure 4.1 says comes first. Answer that, then turn the screen.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record. I'll put that in writing.

Nothing on his record, in writing; I'm writing that down, and I'll want it in an email tonight. A rewrite says there's something wrong with Owen's essay, and you still haven't shown me one page or one date. The zero comes off first, Hale, and then we talk about anything else.
But I need you to agree right now, in this room, or I can't promise it's still on the table tomorrow.

Still on the table tomorrow. Procedure 4.4 gives Owen that option on a first concern, Hale, so it isn't yours to take off the table. Pressure isn't evidence, and I don't sign anything in a room where I haven't seen a single page.
And frankly, you seem like you'd rather win than help him. Prove me wrong.
Prove me wrong. I don't prove anything in this room, Hale; you entered the zero, so the burden is yours. Show me the file with its date, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
